what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted 5-1 to recommend approval of Article 1, the new grade 6-12 Middle High School, for the January 7 Special Town Meeting.
The school building committee presented the options, site plan, costs, financing and homeowner impact, including a do-nothing option and a limited high school renovation.
Financing was presented as 30-year borrowing with a state (MSBA) grant share, and the annual tax impact for average and higher-valued homes was shown.
Members and residents discussed items the state would not reimburse, such as the greenhouse and fields; the greenhouse was described as a removable placeholder.
The committee saw no direct financial impact in the marijuana zoning article and will not discuss it further.

why_it_matters: The article commits the town to long-term borrowing for a new school, so it would show up in property tax bills for decades, and voters at the Special Town Meeting will be asked to decide it.
The final cost to taxpayers depends on the share the state reimburses and on items it does not cover, which is why the greenhouse and fields drew questions.
watch_next: Special Town Meeting on January 7, where Article 1 (the Middle High School) comes to a vote.
Committee's next meeting on January 9, with capital plan finalization targeted for January 2 and fiscal policy work continuing.

The schematic design cost summary was walked through, with the state reimbursement maximum and the town's minimum share; the greenhouse, flooring abatement, utility fees and moving costs fall to the town.
The town manager compared 20-year and 30-year borrowing: the shorter term costs the average household more each year but less in interest.
Existing excluded debt was described as steady and paid off in fiscal 26.
A member is to draft the capital fiscal policy, and the next meeting is set for October 24 at 7 pm.

why_it_matters: The school project would be paid for mostly through a debt exclusion, which raises property tax bills for the life of the loan, so the borrowing term chosen sets both the yearly bill and the total interest.
Costs the state does not reimburse fall to the town, so the town's share depends on what the state excludes as well as on the building's price.
watch_next: Finance Committee meeting October 24 at 7 pm, with fiscal policies and the school building project on the agenda.
The draft capital fiscal policy that a member is to prepare.
